The Reserve Bank of India had first formulated its medium-term strategy framework, viz. ‘Utkarsh 2022’ in July 2019, replacing its annual action plans as the latter spanned over a short period, insufficient to pursue strategic objectives. Continuing the previous two frameworks, Utkarsh 2029 communicates the medium-term strategic priorities of RBI, over a three-year time horizon, Financial Year (FY) 2026-29. UTKARSH 2029

# Page 4^page=4
UTKARSH 2029 Spanning three years from April 2026 to March 2029, Utkarsh 2029 lays down the foundation for following Long Term deliverables: • Project Sa-Mudra for modernising the currency management system, • expanding CBDC for supporting cross- border payments efficient, • scaling up Unified Lending Interface for inclusive credit delivery, • developing frameworks for use of emerging technologies such as AI and Quantum in our financial sector

# Page 5^page=5
UTKARSH 2029 Spanning three years from April 2026 to March 2029, Utkarsh 2029 lays down the foundation for following Long Term deliverables: • Project Sa-Mudra for modernising the currency management system, • expanding CBDC for supporting cross-border payments efficient, • scaling up Unified Lending Interface for inclusive credit delivery, • developing frameworks for use of emerging technologies such as AI and Quantum in our financial sector Utkarsh 2029 continues the long-term deliverables for which the foundation was laid under Utkarsh 2.0 • internationalisation of the INR • UPI to revolutionise cross border payments, etc.

# Page 6^page=6
Structure and Vision Utkarsh 2029 has been fine-tuned to a three-layered structure consisting of strategy pillars, each pillar encompassing a set of deliverables, guided by the vision and values of RBI The Vision statement of Utkarsh 2029 refines the mission, vision and core purpose of the earlier Utkarsh editions: ‘Continue excellence while enabling a stable, inclusive and technologically robust financial system.’

# Page 7^page=7
Values and Actions of RBI Utkarsh 2029 pursues the values of Utkarsh 2022 and Utkarsh 2.0 to guide the actions of RBI

# Page 8^page=8
Strategy Pillars and Deliverables Utkarsh 2029 has been shaped through inputs from Central Office Departments (CODs), Regional Offices (ROs), and RBI subsidiaries to ensure internal inclusivity. The framework is aligned with the Aspirational Goals for RBI@100 and national priorities like Viksit Bharat 2047 and Panch Pran. It comprises 49 deliverables across six strategy pillars, each Pillar representing a key priority of the RBI.

# Page 9^page=9
Medium Term Strategy (2026 - 2029) of RBI Robust Regulation: RBI endeavours to review, rationalise, and simplify instructions periodically and reduce compliance burden for REs, promoting EoDB, minimise procedural redundancies, provide operational flexibility to Regulated Entities, and promote responsible innovation. Customer Centricity and Inclusive Finance: RBI’s strategy focuses on assessing customer service in SCBs, accelerating grievance redressal, enabling grievance escalation. RBI ensures continuous self-assessment through Citizen’s Charter review and publishing a periodic metrics on the same. RBI’s strategy aims at financial inclusion by expanding ULI, reducing lending costs, promoting inclusive credit delivery, and strengthening contagion risk assessment underscoring interconnectedness in financial system.

# Page 10^page=10
Medium Term Strategy (2026 - 2029) of RBI Competitive Markets: This pillar focuses on enhancing market competitiveness and strengthening market infrastructure by automating processes, increasing central clearing for improved operational efficiency, reducing risk, and enhancing market access along with reduce auction turnaround time, price transparency (G- Secs), and expanding retail participation. Effective Technology: The RBI shall leverage technology in various areas of its operations and eliminate paper and / or email-based interactions and ensuring end-to-end digitalisation of internal workflows. The RBI will also deploy tech- driven supervisory tools, develop indigenous AI tools, upgrade systems like e- Kuber 3.0, modernise currency infrastructure and promoting responsible innovation through AI frameworks, sandboxes, and asset tokenisation.

# Page 11^page=11
Medium Term Strategy (2026 - 2029) of RBI Future-ready Organisation: RBI's strategy is to build a future-ready institution through continuous upskilling of resources, reviewing functions across its offices, strengthening two-way communication with its stakeholders, and embedding sustainability and climate awareness in its actions and decisions to further institutional excellence. Global India: The Bank aims to enhance global cooperation by promoting UPI adoption abroad, expanding INR-based int trade settlement, expanding cross- border CBDC arrangements, and adopting global standards to enhance global competitiveness. It aims to actively pursue the leadership role India could play in different international discourses.

# Page 14^page=14
Q2. With reference to the strategy pillars and focus areas under Utkarsh 2029 of the Reserve Bank of India, consider the following statements: 1. Robust Regulations focus on simplification and resilience. 2. Customer Centricity and Inclusive Finance emphasize accessibility and interconnectedness. 3. Competitive Markets aim at financial deepening and digitisation. 4. Effective Technology focuses on financial inclusion and sustainability. 5. Future-ready Organisation emphasizes profitability and revenue maximisation. 6. Global India focuses on standardisation and internationalisation. Which of the statements given above are correct? A. 1, 2, 3 and 6 only B. 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 only C. 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 only D. 1, 3, 4 and 6 only E. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 MCQs for Practice
